chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no omission (of obligatory acts) in the Maghrib and Fajr prayers.

key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Omission or forgetfulness of an obligatory act during prayer

ai.seo_question: Are the Maghrib and Fajr prayers exempt from forgetfulness (sahw) of obligatory acts?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that the short prayers of Maghrib and Fajr do not permit the omission of obligatory acts (*fara'id*) due to forgetfulness, requiring their compensation. This contrasts with longer prayers like Dhuhr and Asr, where *sahw* allows for temporary omission, highlighting the strictness applied to the brevity of these two specific prayers. The ruling underscores the principle that the structural integrity of the prayer is preserved even in shorter durations, ensuring no pillar is left unperformed.
